text_fidelity_a:
Battat - Deluxe Wooden Train – Classic Toy Train Set with Magnetic Trains, Tracks, Vehicles, Buildings & Accessories for Kids Aged 3 & Up (102Pc), Fits Thomas, Brio, Chuggington Trains are a classic toy. Most of them are electronic, high- tech in nature, and can be made to look and sound like an authentic train, in small scale of course. But there is also something to be said for a train that isn’t electronic and requires imagination more than anything. This is what you get with the Battat Deluxe Wooden Train.

This train set comes with track, train, and a large number of accessories. It’s easy to assemble the track because it interlocks with almost no effort. Setting up the accessories takes time, but this is perfect for the more imaginative child and parents will enjoy just sitting back and letting their youngster take over.

The quality level of this set is good and the pieces are made from wood. Once assembled, it covers about four feet by three feet of space, so it will fit on most tables. If you don’t have available table space to spare, just set it up on the floor instead. A smooth surface is best, of course, but a flat carpet may work, too.

With the train cars, they are held together by magnets and this is good enough for this type of train. One issue some people may have is with the track. The interlocking isn’t very secure and that means the track is easy to bump out of place. Metal tracks hold together better, but this isn’t a huge issue, really. Most kids won’t mind this aspect of the set up.

There are some really cool electronic trains on the market, but trains that require manual movements and that lack sound and other automated features can be just as fun. The Battat Deluxe Wooden Train is good for this purpose. It’s made with a good deal of quality in mind and it’s great for stimulating a child’s imagination.
text_fidelity_b: Battat - Deluxe Wooden Train – Classic Toy Train Set with Magnetic Trains, Tracks, Vehicles, Buildings & Accessories for Kids Aged 3 & Up (102Pc), Fits Thomas, Brio, Chuggington

text_fidelity_a:
3Doodler Start Essentials 3D Pen Set For Kids with Free Refill Filament - STEM Toy For Boys & Girls, Age 6 & Up - Toy of The Year Award Winner I think this thing is awesome!

That said, I do have a couple of warnings to consider. First, it will get really expensive! The sticks don't go very far at all. (The package claims each 6 inch stick will give you 60 inches of play, so I'm going to assume we just need more practice to get that much, as I'm guessing most others will, too.) With this set, you'll get 2 packs of the sticks(48 total sticks...6 each of white, mint green, yellow, orange, blue, red, green, and grey). You'll use those up super quick! These sticks are biodegradable, BPA-free and labeled as "safe". From what I've read, you'll need these specific sticks to go with the 3Doodler.

Also, every time you put a new color stick through the pen, you'll be wasting a bit of the previous stick, unless it works into your design. The whole stick won't completely feed through until you put another one in there to push it on out.

It takes a great deal of practice to get anything worthwhile to turn out. I have 3 little boys and they all want a chance at practicing, so even more sticks are used up in that process. So far, we haven't came up with anything close to what is shown in the practice book, but none of us can call ourselves overly skilled in the artistic realm at this point in time.

All of that said, IF your budget allows for buying lots of sticks to go with this pen, it truly is awesome! (Or you could request packs of these sticks as grandparent presents for the kids.) ;) Letting a child use his/her imagination with this thing is an amazing opportunity, and I definitely recommend it. (I even recommend it for adults, too, because we all need a little childish fun every once in awhile!)

It's easy to use. Just charge it up with the included micro USB cable(or do like me and use your kindle charger), turn it on and wait for the light to turn green. Then, press the button to start it and press it again to stop it. Simple! As I mentioned earlier, there is a book with instructions and some ideas to practice and get started with the pen. There's no worries about getting burned. I tested it out, and while the plastic is a little warm when it first comes out, it's not even close to hot. This allows for a little wiggle room for moving around your design before it completely dries.

In the end, other than the sticks being a costly investment, this is a great little invention, and we've loved it so far!
text_fidelity_b: 3Doodler Start Essentials 3D Pen Set For Kids with Free Refill Filament - STEM Toy For Boys & Girls, Age 6 & Up - Toy of The Year Award Winner

text_fidelity_a:
Enso Rings Disney Lilo & Stitch Silicone Ring Collection - Comfortable and Flexible Design - Ohana and Experiment 626 I wear a silicone ring and truly like it. Perhaps prefer it because I don't worry about it like I do gold or silver, nor do I tend to hook it (sometimes painfully) on things. I recently noticed the Enso Rings Collections and liked much of what I saw, so when I spotted this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection available I grabbed it. In this case, for my wife. I am a Disney fan as well, but Stitch is one of her favorites, and honestly, I was not a big fan of the red - I prefer blue or black in silicone and the traditional silvers and golds. So... how would we like this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection?

1. It arrived in a nice little packaging making great for protecting the ring, displaying the ring, and a nice presentation for gifting. Great all around.

2. Sizing. Honestly, this was the hardest part. Sizing your finger is never the easiest of tasks as we have discovered. But in this case they wanted the inside of a ring rather than your finger. We have a flexible, cloth type measuring tape, but still, trying to get that in there and with the metal end and lined up and staying in place as you pull it out.. not fun. They do have their sizes to the rounded whole - I feel like I remember others with in between sizes, which would make this harder. In the end we went with the one we got consistently and hoped. Turned out great - fits my wife's middle finger as she wanted and my ring finger.

3. The red is actually pretty cool. Again, not my favorite on the spectrum of ring colors, but my wife loves it and I like it. And for the Lilo and Stitch option, it works. There is a sparkle to it - both nice and not overwhelming.

4. The in-print on the ring feels "subtle," but present; something you can see, but at a glance it's more like a light-shadow affect. Upon closer examination you spot the little Lilo (not a fave character for either of us), but the Stitch rocks. And the little flower brings out the Polynesian flavor, while giving the whole thing a sweet nod to Disney. For a Disney fan, it's a great find.

5. This is my wife's first silicone, but like me, she's liking it. It is comfortable, easy to wear, does not catch on things in the same way (but all rings do catch), and it has that silicone flexibility that makes wearing it more comfortable in many situations.

6. I have found in wearing silicone I have to be more careful when washing my hands. Soap can build up behind and/or keep up the wetness between ring and finger, and can come off easier when drying. I warned her and sure enough, same thing. So do be careful. Additionally, she finds there is a (slight) risk of stuff like soap building up in the little grooves. No worries, what little she thinks she saw (it's tiny) washed out easily. And so far, after two weeks, it continues to look like new.

In the end she really likes this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection and is so happy to have this Stitch ring. I've seen a few others on their pages I'd consider, so yes, we'd get another Enso ring. Always fun to wear an ode to something that makes you smile.
text_fidelity_b: Enso Rings Disney Lilo & Stitch Silicone Ring Collection - Comfortable and Flexible Design - Ohana and Experiment 626

Then you win or lose based on your guess. The game is quick enough that even small kids (2 years old) stay interested in the game. ALEX Discover Tots Art Gallery The best part of this kit is the portfolio! It's been an awesome collection spot for prepackaged(whether by me or someone else)art projects. My 3 and 5 year old can just grab themselves a project and work on them together. Sometimes I've helped, but other times not. It's a great way to teach a little independence, and give this mama a moment of peace. ;) It's also been great for organizing projects for my 3 year old to work on while his older brothers do schoolwork. My goal has been to simplify for more peace, and this little kit has been a blessing in that goal.

Of course, you can use the portfolio to organize finished projects, but I typically throw stuff like this in the garbage after the newness has worn off. I only keep the more original, creative things my children create, and these project aren't original or overly creative. Sometimes easy projects like this are just what a child(and mommy/daddy/other person in charge) needs, though, and I appreciate having them around.

As far as art projects, you'll get 12 separate pages. Some are for coloring, some for putting stickers on, and many of them are sticky pages. (You'll pull paper off, leaving a sticky part. It will hold paper or shapes or buttons without the worry and mess of glue.) It also comes with various shapes and sizes of paper for sticking on pages, colors, buttons, and stickers. *Note: In one of the other kits from Alex Jr., the whole sticky part came off while trying to pull the paper off. My kids were disappointed, but that page can then just be used as a sticker page or coloring page. My youngest two highly prefer the sticky pages, though!

Overall, this is a nice kit! It's been a blessing to have a few "busy" projects around.

text_fidelity_a:
Games The Original Tiny Hands Challenge Well first, this game is absolutely ridiculous. Some of the challenges with the hands are near to impossible. But it did exactly what we hoping for at our last family reunion. It got several families blended into the fun and laughing hysterically, even those who had just driven 12 hours. The premise is easy, you have to do everything with Tiny or Tinier fake hands from catching a ball to acting out charades. The rules are simple although the rules of betting and scoring were less than clear to us. To be honest, we pretty much abandoned the betting and scoring of each round and just played the cards and the spinner. In the end we just declared the kids the winners.

Some things we learned.
- Put the score card well out of harms way. Ours was trod upon and score pieces were constantly tossed around.
- You cannot hold onto a pen with the hands like a baseball bat and swing it without impaling someone with the pen
- Give yourself lots of room
- The Charades part went over best.

Not sure how often this will come out, but it is a great leveler of ages and abilities and plays well in groups as long as kids are eight and up. It is kinetic, laugh producing and fun.
text_fidelity_b: Games The Original Tiny Hands Challenge

text_fidelity_a:
ETA hand2mind Connecting People, Set of 96 This educational toy consists of small, easily swallowed pieces, making it a choking hazard. Thus, it is not recommended for children younger than age 5 and should be kept well away from pets, especially puppies who like to chew things. This toy is recommended for grades K-4, which is approximately ages 5-9. It's primary purpose is helping children learn counting. They can also use it to learn to sort and classify.

The set includes 96 pieces of sturdy, plastic, free-standing, girl and boy figures. Half are male and half female. The pieces come in three sizes, each in four colors, yellow, red, green and blue. The sizes are all rather small, ranging from only 1/2 inch to 1 inch in height. The larger figures weigh about 3-4 grams and the smallest figures weigh about 1 gram. The figures are well made in terms of having smooth surfaces, which is important to avoid harming small fingers. The figures are stored in a zip-lock type plastic bag.

As advertised, the pieces do stand up by themselves, and they can be linked together. However, it can be difficult for younger children to clip them together. They each have a protruding peg on one hand and a hole on the other hand. It takes hand-eye coordination to match up a peg and a hole, and some finger strength to shove a peg into a hole. Taking them apart is even harder. Thus, this toy can be frustrating to kids on the younger end of the recommended age range, 5-6 years old, and is most likely to be handled smoothly by children on the higher end of the scale, age 7-9. Some of these problems might have been avoided if the figures came in larger sizes.
text_fidelity_b: ETA hand2mind Connecting People, Set of 96

Jurassic World Toys , Research Lab Fisher-Price Imaginext toys in general are great toys. Durable, bright colored plastic that often take after popular shows and movies such as Batman and Superman, Power Rangers, or in this case, Jurassic World. These toys have allowed my son's imagination to run wild and be creative as he plays for many hours with these. We often play together, but for the most part he's very happy to play with these on his own for hours at a time. I probably purchased my first Imaginext toy about 3 years ago, Batman and his Batcycle. It has held up to the test of time and a very rough preschooler. My son is now 6 with multiple sets.

Jurassic World has been all the rage in my house this summer because little boys love dinosaurs and that is certainly true of mine! So, take his love for Imaginext toys and mix that with his love for dinos and it's the perfect mashup! The only caveat is that on Amazon I have found the prices to vary greatly from in stores. Toys R Us (R.I.P.) was a great source for Imaginext because they always had the best and lowest price on these. They also had more selections. So, I would caution anyone to first look around Target or Walmart first. I once bought Batgirl and her Batcopter for $30 on Amazon and it was in Toys R Us for $15. I regularly see Imaginext toys in Target selling for $5-10 cheaper than on Amazon.

With the Fisher Price Imaginext Jurassic World Research Lab you get one T-Rex, one scientist, one harpoon, and one claw. There is a "decontamination" chamber for the scientist to get clean to study his subject. Simply turn the powerpad and the blue decontamination spiral gets the scientist ready. There is a powerpad to open and close the cage for the T-Rex. But watch out! The T-Rex might get loose! the lab is not that big. It's smaller than all of the Batcaves I've ever purchased. It's no bigger than any of the Paw Patrol sets I've purchased as well. So, it's east to tuck it away in a corner. All of the pieces, including the T-Rex, we've placed in a plastic show box for organization and storage. Overall, it's a fun play-set that provides hours of entertainment and keeps kids away from screens!
text_fidelity_b: Jurassic World Toys , Research Lab

Toysmith Euler's Disk This works ok.  The disc is metal and very heavy.  But the plastic base for the mirror is far too flimsy and lightweight to accommodate the disc without a lot of flexing and popping and clapping noise.  All of this  means lost energy which reduces spin time.  The product just doesn't implement well the design the patent describes.

I wanted to better stabilize the base, so under running hot water I very carefully removed the mirror from the base.  Perhaps not something I would recommend.  As I was doing so, the smell of whatever adhesive was used literally made me light-headed.  I've used a lot of epoxies and adhesives, but none that smelled as strong as this, like really strong gasoline.  The adhesive was soft and spongy, not fully cured.  I carefully removed all of  whatever it was and filled the gap between the base and the bottom of the mirror with air-dry clay to fill the gaps and to increase the weight of the base overall.  It did help to increase spin time somewhat and got rid of the annoying galloping-horse-playing-steel-drum sounds.

text_fidelity_a: Barbie Dreamtopia Sweetville Kingdom Carriage I have been a Barbie fan since I was a child, many years ago. My now 16 year old daughter was a huge fan when she was young. I even have several "in the box" collector Barbies. The Barbie Dreamtopia Sweetville Kingdom Carriage just doesn't seem as high quality as the many Barbie products I have purchased over the years. It's definitely not a collector's item. The price is decent and you get a complete set of a doll, unicorn, and carriage. The plastic carriage flexes when you apply pressure. It doesn't feel like it's going to easily break, but it's not as rigid as other Barbie products. The carriage door opens and closes.  The wheels rotate easily and give a pretty smooth ride. The details on the carriage are nice. There are lots of textures to make it more realistic.  The unicorn is a sturdier plastic piece. The doll has the rigid, no bend legs. Her facial details are what you expect on Barbies. She has a removable crown. Her top is molded plastic and not removable. Her skirt is a cute, candy print fabric, but the material itself is stiff and doesn't flow or move. In fact, I don't like the skirt at all. Overall, it's an attractive looking set, but the quality is disappointing. With all that said, I think young Barbie fans would probably still enjoy it.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Dreamtopia Sweetville Kingdom Carriage

text_fidelity_a:
Pathfinder Adventure Card Game: Wrath of the Righteous Base Set We hold a monthly “Game Night” at our house and felt this was the perfect opportunity to introduce the Pathfinder Card game to our friends. Unfortunately, it took at least two hours to explain the rules of the game and our crowd is mostly people over 40, so keeping track of each character’s journey, remembering what powers they do or do not have, and explaining strategy was somewhat difficult, especially as everyone was a first time player. I think this game is best suited to a younger crowd (under 40) but it’s still fun for those who really stick with it.

A few of us played Dungeons & Dragons years ago, so this playing this felt very familiar. Every player is given the opportunity to "customize" their game play, in that they can choose to be a particular character. The characters are individually possessed of different powers, spells, weapons, and capabilities. You choose a specific character and a “scenerio” (a.k.a storyline) and draw cards that determine the path of your journey. Your objective is to maximize your advantage, using the cards and dice to advance or retreat. The objective, of course, is to win the game by overcoming monsters and capturing the bad guys for points. It’s like a video game in that they are different levels and you can move on to different stages. The game shifts scenes as you advance, so it feels like a continual maze. The game can technically go on forever as the company encourages you to buy “expansion sets” that give you additional cards and new adventures to go on.

Two people in our group are big science fiction and fantasy buffs, and they absolutely loved it. text_fidelity_a: Disney Colorbrain, The Ultimate Board Game for Families who Love Disney This game is harder than you might think. I thought my Disney knowledge was pretty good, but I was stumped on maybe 1/3 of the questions during the two games I played. My younger Disneyphiles did about the same as me. You might remember that the caterpillar in Alice in Wonderland is blue, but can you recall the color of the flags that sit atop the hats of the Tweedles? There are some questions that require you to come up with as many as five different colors, all of which must be correct for you to gain a point. What color is Celia's dress from Monsters Inc? What three colors are seen in Go Go Tomago's superhero suit from Big Hero 6?  You need to answer quickly, by putting down your selected color cards in front of you. This is actually pretty fun and interesting. Minor characters can be especially tricky. There were a few cards with answers that we disagreed with, such as the one that said Joy from Inside Out wore a yellow dress, when we all see it as green. The answer cards all have pictures from the animated films, and sometimes the photo is not great quality. My family enjoyed this game despite these issues and found it a more challenging activity than we had anticipated. It takes almost no time to learn how to set up and play. You can fill ten minutes or half an hour easily.
text_fidelity_b: Disney Colorbrain, The Ultimate Board Game for Families who Love Disney

I’m in it now, and I can say this is one of the most poorly formulated puzzles I’ve ever done. It appears that whoever decided the pattern of the piece cut outs was lazy and decided to have repeating shapes throughout, which results in many perfect fits that are completely incorrect. In places where the differences are obvious, it’s not much of an issue, but there are also plenty of times this happens in areas that look similar, resulting in incorrect placement, backtracking, and frustration. I love puzzles, but not this one. I love friends, but I can’t stand this friends puzzle. The visual design was excellent, so whoever came up with that did a wonderful job. Lots of nostalgia, lots of little visual cues to make it fun. But whoever designed the cut out portion did an awful job.

Deep Dilemmas - 'Would You Rather' Conversation Cards for Ridiculous Debates & Funny Interactions. 200 Original Ice Breaker Question Cards for Adults, Couples, & College Students - Ages 16+ I've picked up a bunch of these conversation starter games and some are better than others. I would say this one is right down the middle. It's a very straightforward concept - on each card is two choices and you're supposed to pick each one. The problem is that maybe half of them are real dilemmas, while the other half are no brainers. For instance - "would you rather live on a 50th floor penthouse with no elevator or have $2 million in dimes". These are the kinds of questions that might as well not be there because everyone just picks one of the answers and there's no discussion needed, which defeats the point of the game. In some ways I feel like they knew this going in - on the side of the box, it's actually printed that the playtime is up to 60 minutes - with 200 cards, that averages out to 3 cards per minute.

I packed it all up and put in for a return.  There are a lot of websites that HIGHLY recommend this drone- I have a feeling they are paid for this as this thing is truly unusable. Each model (e.g., crane, helicopter) actually works, and is accompanied by a “what's happening here” explanation in the manual of why it works (e.g., turning a crank hoists a crane load by exerting force on a rope threaded through pulleys that share the weight to be lifted; a helicopter’s fast tail rotor produces a force that counteracts the main rotor’s force to stabilize the helicopter).

The models are assembled from plastic parts (some parts are similar to LEGO Technic elements) by following clear step-by-step diagrams (similar to LEGO building instructions). They are powered by a pressurized air tank controlled by a switch with a lever. There are no batteries to buy or charge, because you pressurize the air tank by pumping air into it (the pump assembly resembles a bicycle tire pump).

Each model has suggestions for finding out more about the scientific principles that relate to it. The manual indicates the difficulty level of each model with a three-dot system (easy, medium, difficult).

This kit may seem expensive (about $90 on Amazon), but it teaches a LOT about the practical application of physical and engineering principles, for the price of a single medium-sized LEGO Technic kit. It's a kit to use in home schooling, or to give to a child who really wants to understand why and how construction equipment, vehicles, watercraft, aircraft, and cameras work in the real world.

Craft-tastic – String Art Kit – Craft Kit Makes One 3D String Art Heart This CRAFT-TASTIC 3D STRING ART KIT provides an inexpensive (about $6.25 on Amazon) introduction to the string art craft. It includes a snap-together plastic frame, plenty of colored embroidery floss for string, and reasonably clear instructions. The box says it's for ages 8 and up, which seems about right. (Adult help might be needed to assemble the frame, which requires the pegs to be properly oriented upwards or downwards for everything to snap together tightly.)

There is some artistic creativity involved with this kit, as there are no stringing diagrams to follow. Instead, the instructions say to knot your string to a peg in the frame, and then "wrap the thread from a peg in one (upper) heart to a peg on the other side (the lower heart)." This is simple enough, but it's up to you to choose the pegs so that you get an eye-pleasing criss-crossing of the thread.

Personally, I don't care for the color combinations: bright blue small inside heart, purple edge for the large outside heart, yellow front of large outside heart, pink back of large outside heart. When you're finished with all the stringing, you can set the big heart up on a little plastic stand.

A small child might enjoy this project a lot. However, being an adult, I was bored by the time I'd finished the small blue heart. Because this kit persuaded me that I don't care for the string art craft, I rate it at 3 stars ("It's okay" on the official Amazon scale). However, the budget price probably makes it a reasonable purchase if the intent is to keep a small child busy.

Horrible Guild Similo Fables: A Fast-Playing Family Card Game - Guess the Secret Fairy Tale Character, 2-8 Players, Ages 8+, 20 min I'd never heard of Similo before, but there are other varieties of this card game(History and Myths...in June, at least). They can even be mixed with this one for a different game and there are instructions for doing so in this deck. The game is pretty simple. There's a Clue Giver and the other players are Guessers. The Clue Giver picks one of the characters in the deck(putting it back afterwards, along with 11 other cards) and then uses only cards leftover to give clues(5 cards in hand at a time), with no words or gestures. The 12 cards for the Guessers are spread in a grid and the Clue Giver gives one card per round for a clue. Vertical means there's something similar to the Secret Character and horizontal means there's something different. For example, if I'm the Clue Giver and I picked Aladdin, I could put Genie vertically, since they're from the same tale or I could put Cheshire Cat horizontally, since Aladdin isn't an animal. It's up the the Clue Giver to decide what's similar or different. The game is over within 5 rounds. The Guessers take away one card for the first round, two for the second, etc. If the Secret Character is taken away, the game is over, but if the final card is the Secret Character, the Guessers win.

I like that this game is cooperative. My children have to work together to win the game. We have plenty of competitive games, but very few cooperative ones, so this is a nice feature for us. I also like the illustrations on the cards. They're brightly colored and well done. It also doesn't take long to play, so if short on time, it's a nice way to pass just a bit of time and still have fun.
text_fidelity_b: Horrible Guild Similo Fables: A Fast-Playing Family Card Game - Guess the Secret Fairy Tale Character, 2-8 Players, Ages 8+, 20 min

LEGO Batman Movie - Batman LED Torch Night Light/Reading Light - 8 in My son is pleased. I am happy that he is happy, but probably should have given this a pass. Lego Batman the Night Light arrives with batteries, but it takes AA's so have them on hand and a Phillips head screwdriver to open the battery compartment door. Batman looks and feels just the regular tiny Lego Batman. The only difference aside from the size are the lights in his feet. Cape, cowl, smirk are all the same. In order to use it, Batman must either be sitting down for full use of the lights or in a semi-split position with one foot forward. The light is not bright enough to use solely as a reading light and the LED is a bit harsh as a night light. My son is happy with it, so what do I care, but I just wish it either had a brighter light for reading, or a softer light for sleeping. Batman turns on with a button on his "9-pack" and stays on for 30 mins. Just enough time to read a story or two and go to sleep. Batman when seated is about the size of a tall coffee mug (Starbucks mug size).

I am also very disappointed with delivery on this. I ordered it about two weeks before Christmas, was told it would arrive prior to and I did not receive it until after New Years. I had to explain to my 5 year old that Santa forgot something and sent it. Because I knew my son would love I did not cancel the order, but again shipping on this was extremely disappointing.
